result.title: MEA: A Reward-Driven Multi-Agent System for Faithful Model Explanations
result.summary: Recent years have seen the employment of a plethora of machine learning (ML) models in high-stakes domains, but they remain largely opaque to the practitioners who act on their predictions. While post-hoc explanation methods offer a lens into this model behavior, wielding them effectively demands expertise most domain experts lack: navigating high-dimensional outputs, selecting the best explanations, and synthesizing evidence across disparate tools. To this end, we present MEA, a multi-agent framework that removes the explanation knowledge barrier entirely: a Proposer agent selects and configures explanation tools based on the question and modality, while an Actor agent is optimized end-to-end against faithfulness, transforming the outputs into natural language explanations grounded in model behavior across tabular, text, and vision modalities. Further, we introduce diverse question types spanning feature attribution, counterfactual reasoning, and spurious feature detection, each paired with a perturbation-based faithfulness metric. We find that frontier LLMs systematically produce unfaithful explanations. By optimizing against faithfulness rewards augmented with a modality-adaptive penalty, MEA consistently outperforms post hoc explainers, agentic, and closed-source baselines across six datasets, with reward-driven optimization yielding faithfulness gains of +28% (tabular), +21% (text), and +34% (vision) over the untrained backbone. More broadly, our findings suggest that AI agents themselves can serve as a scalable, adaptable interface to ML explainability, opening a path toward natural-language explainability that generalizes beyond the fixed, single-purpose tools that have long defined the field.

AI.brief_summary: MEA 提出一个奖励驱动的多智能体框架，由 Proposer 选择并配置解释工具、Actor 以忠实度奖励端到端优化，将表格、文本和视觉模型的行为输出转化为自然语言解释，并配套基于扰动的忠实度指标与多类问题（特征归因、反事实、虚假特征检测）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「忠实度奖励＋扰动验证」的信号设计及工具选择、证据合成流程，可能与 LVR 中答案是否真正使用 latent 内容、视觉证据筛选与贡献分配的监督方式相关，可供核查是否可迁移为 latent 轨迹的忠实度判据。
